SMTO-LLM-0045 — SMTO couldn't tell which tool the model picked

GUID: ed67ddba-6ac1-4f96-a4fa-52f2c7e32476
Slug: ambiguous-tool-name
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • The model sent the tool's name in pieces, and those pieces could spell two different tools that both exist. SMTO didn't run either one, since picking the wrong tool could do the wrong thing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait to see whether the Run continues. SMTO may ask the model once more by itself after a reply it can't use. The tool name may come through clearly on the model's next try.
  2. If the Run stopped, read its activity in the conversation to see which steps already finished, then ask the Agent to continue only the rest. Neither tool was run, but steps before it already happened. Repeating them could do the same work twice.
  3. If it keeps happening, ask the person who runs the model server to check how it streams tool requests, or choose a different model in Settings › Setup › Model routing. This mix-up comes from how the model server sends the tool name in pieces.

What success looks like

  • The Run continues past this step, and the Agent's next action appears in its activity.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the model server or manages SMTO. Don't ask the Agent to redo steps that already finished.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Streamed tool-name fragments resolve to two different advertised tool names (joined incremental pieces versus the final cumulative piece).

What this means

  • Tool-name fragments admit conflicting advertised names under cumulative versus incremental reconstruction. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Tool-name fragments admit conflicting advertised names under cumulative versus incremental reconstruction.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare fragment encoding with the available exact tool names; check the provider's cumulative-versus-delta convention.

How to fix it

  • Raised by reconstruct_name in src/agent_runtime/llm/openai_compat/response.py. Fix the provider's streaming tool-call parser so function.name is sent once or consistently as incremental pieces; check the raw name fragments in the trace and do not pick a name heuristically.
  • Use the advertised exact tool name and repair the provider’s tool parser if it emits conflicting names.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The same stream resolves to one advertised tool name without competing interpretations.

What not to do

  • Do not replay prior successful operations to repair a later model response.
  • Do not disable protocol validation or treat this representation failure as input-context overflow.
